comments.quote_zh: 我强烈推荐下面这个 CGP Grey 的视频，它更详细地讲了 First Past the Post 投票的问题
comments.text_zh: 我强烈推荐下面这个 CGP Grey 的视频，它更详细地讲了 First Past the Post（简单多数制）投票的问题（[视频]）。> 但我们的制度恰恰是 FPTP，为什么？因为这是最简单、最幼稚的选举制度，连 Joe Bloggs 都能看懂。它就是“得票最多的人赢”。这个制度造成的问题都是转瞬即逝的统计问题，要解释清楚、甚至要察觉到它们正在发生，都不是十秒钟的一句话能办到的。所以从 Joe Bloggs 的角度看，你是在凭你的脑力劳动得出结论说错误的人可能赢得选举，就想改变他与生俱来的投票权。2011 年英国 Alternative Vote（排序复选制）公投失败，就是这么回事。
comments.text: I highly recommend the following CGP Grey video for further detail about the problems of First Past the Post voting ( [VIDEO] ). > But instead we have FPTP, and why? Its the simplest and most naive electoral system so Joe Bloggs understands it. Its just "the person who gets the most votes wins". The problems this system causes are ephemeral statistical problems that require more than a 10 second soundbite to explain or even to detect happening. So from Joe Bloggs point of view, you want to change his fundamental right to vote based on the fact that your intellectual busywork has concluded that the wrong person can win the election. That's how the UK failed to get Alternative Vote passed in 2011.

comments.quote_zh: First-past-the-post 投票模型已经失灵，几乎必然导致两党制
comments.text_zh: First-past-the-post 投票模型已经失灵，几乎必然导致两党制：选民必须策略性地投票给他们并不支持的候选人，以避免自己最不喜欢的候选人获胜。例如，你可能更认同 Bernie Sanders 的政策，但如果你认为 Hillary 在对阵 Trump 时胜算更大，你仍然会投给 Hillary。或者你可能更偏好其他共和党候选人，但想避免 Trump 以独立候选人身份参选、分裂选民基础，从而把胜利送给民主党。我认为这是现行制度的巨大问题：缺乏自己认同的候选人会让人幻灭，并停止投票。[VIDEO]
comments.text: The first-past-the-post voting model is broken and virtually guarantees a two-party system where voters must vote strategically for candidates they don't support to avoid their least-preferred candidate winning. For instance, you may prefer Bernie Sander's policies but still vote Hillary if you think she will have a better chance against Trump in the election. Or you may prefer other Republican candidates, but want to avoid Trump going independent, splitting the voter base and handing the victory to the Democrats. I think this is a huge problem with the current system, as the lack of candidates they agree with make people get disillusioned and stop voting. [VIDEO]

comments.text_zh: 我先从我的原型开始：[LINK] 有人对选举方法或博弈论感兴趣吗？如果你看过 CGP Grey 关于选举方法的视频，或者看过 Nicky Case 的《To Build a Better Ballot》[1]，那这个项目非常符合那种精神。它主要是个玩具，会用大量不同的选举方法跑一场单一的选举。目前我已经实现了大约 26 种不同的选举方法，还挺不错的。不过，我一直回避投票理论爱好者最喜欢的那类方法：Condorcet 方法。我实现了 Copeland（虽然有个错误我还没修），以及 Kemeny Young。但 Kemeny Young 是用最暴力的方式实现的，现在是 O(n!)。我想我主要是在找有数学/博弈论背景、愿意帮忙的人，但任何感兴趣的人都欢迎。我知道 Kemeny Young 算法有很多可以优化的地方，但我一直犹豫，因为我找不到合适的定理来确保某些假设成立。比如，我很确定弱 Condorcet 获胜者的某个子集会位于获胜路径的前端，但我没找到哪本教科书明确这么说过，而且我大学毕业已经很久了，所以自己证明给自己看有点没底。我也不认为每次都要重新学一遍证明、只为确认我的假设在数学上站得住脚，是开发这种工具的最佳方式。谢谢 全部开源……
comments.text: I'll start off with my prototype: [LINK] Anyone into electoral methods or game theory? If you've ever watched CGP Grey's videos on electoral methods or seen Nicky Case's *To Build a Better Ballot*,[1] it's very much in the spirit of that. It's mostly a toy that will run a single election in a large number of different electoral methods. Currently I've implemented ~26 different electoral methods which is pretty neat. However, I've shied away from the methods that voting theory nerds love the most: Condorcet methods. I've implemented Copeland (although there's a mistake I haven't fixed yet) as well as Kemeny Young. However, Kemeny Young is implemented in the most brute force way possible and is O(n!) right now. Mostly I think I'm just looking for people with a math/game-theory background that would be interested in helping out, but I'm open to anyone interested. I know there's a lot of optimizations I could make to the Kemeny Young algorithm, but I've been hesitant to do so because I can't find the right theorems to make sure certain assumptions are true. For example, I'm quite sure that a subset of weak Condorcet winners would be at the front of the winning path, but I haven't found a textbook that's stated this explicitly and it's been a long time since college so I'm kinda iffy on proving it to myself. I also don't think having to learn the proof everytime just to make sure my assumptions are mathematically sound is the best way to develop such a tool. Thanks It's all open-s
